question: An article is marked at ₹2,000. A shopkeeper offers a discount of 25% on the article. What is the selling price of the article after the discount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A 25% discount means the Selling Price is 75% of the Marked Price.

Fraction value of 75% = 3/4

SP = 3/4 × ₹2000

SP = 3 × ₹500 = ₹1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹2000

Discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

Discount = MP × (Discount % ÷ 100)

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 MP = ₹2000
 (100%)
 
 
 
• 
 − 25% Discount
 (− ₹500)
 
 
 
 SP = ₹1500
 (75%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount amount = 2000 × (25 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount amount = 2000 × (1 ÷ 4) = ₹500

⇒ Selling Price = 2000 − 500 = ₹1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is an allowance given to the buyer and is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) or List Price of an article.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of A% and B% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is calculated as: A + B − (A × B ÷ 100).

Profit and Loss Calculation

While Discount is applied to the Marked Price, Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the original Cost Price (CP) of the item.
